result.scientific_strategy:
## c92ccfe2-1135-4ec4-bc5a-eded729fc461 / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The human objective is at least 196 successes out of 200 official episodes on the unchanged full-range reach-and-hold task. The evidence-backed working and best-known policy, checkpoint-100352, achieved 1945/2000 = 97.25% over two disjoint 1000-episode full-range panels, with 99.5% on the reused seed-5000 panel and 98.0% on the reused task-reference panel. Later working controls reached 98.6% and 97.0% on seeds 11000 and 12000, so the larger development evidence still falls short of the objective. The residual is angularly localized rather than radial: success is 72.9% in [-150,-120) and 96.6% in [-180,-150), while every other 30-degree bin is perfect in the pooled baseline panels. Of 55 pooled baseline failures, 28 never entered tolerance and 27 entered but held fewer than 50 steps. A fresh unchanged run reached only 15.1% and 17.4%, and the feasible-IK reward challengers reached 96.9-97.0% without reducing the same lower-left failures.

**Lessons and limits:** The 14-20 cm training annulus was not the binding gap: 6-14 cm targets generalize at about 97.6%, no worse than trained bands. Extended training of the same recipe gave no measured gain: checkpoint-100352 beats checkpoint-120832 on a shared 1000-episode panel (97.2% versus 96.2%) and every paired comparison (12-1 over 1200 episodes); checkpoints 115712 and 105472 also remain behind. Training proxies plateaued while measured failures stayed angularly structured, and proxy peaks for both challengers did not predict task success. The 50% lower-left curriculum, full hold-progress forfeiture, and feasible-IK reward interventions did not produce durable gains. The 11-value observation exposes both analytic IK branches, but code inspection shows that one branch can violate the +/-170 degree joint limits in the residual sector while the other remains feasible; this is a plausible representation mechanism, not measured causal evidence. Reward-only changes preserve the existing policy I/O and can use transfer, while a branch-feasibility representation changes the observation contract and requires fresh learning; unchanged tensor dimensions would not establish semantic compatibility. The fresh result demonstrates substantial process variance but does not quantify it. Large research panels are development evidence with selection context, the task-reference panel is reused, and angular decompositions are descriptive. Experiment 2 is invalid and unmeasured, so its attempted curriculum change is neither a positive nor negative result. These limits distinguish the campaign decisions: more same-recipe training, another fresh-process study, semantically compatible reward changes, and a new representation contract are not interchangeable routes.

**Open questions:** It remains uncertain whether the lower-left never-enter failures are primarily optimization errors, confusion between analytic IK branches, or the joint-limit geometry exposed by those branches. It also remains uncertain whether hold-boundary oscillation is stable across recipes and how much fresh-initialization variance the single failed replication represents. The possible outcomes bear on different decisions: whether to invest in a semantically compatible reward or curriculum change, whether a new representation contract is warranted, and whether process variance merits more training. These are provisional uncertainties for reassessment, not a prescribed action or experiment queue.
